caveats: Lisa Jordan assembled the Nigeria data set, but the original source is FEWS NET.  Please acknowledge FEWS.net for present and historical data using the IPC system to classify acute food security.  Consult FEWS NET or IPCInfo for documentation on appropriate display of IPC classes.
methodology_other:
FEWS.net distributes current and historial shapefiles that characterize regions of program countries on the basis of IPC acute food security classification.  These categories include: 1 - Minimal, 2 - Stressed, 3 - Crisis, 4 - Emergency, and 5 - Famine.  The most recent Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) data sets can be found at: http://www.fews.net/data.  Information about the IPC can be found at: http://www.ipcinfo.org/.

1) Historical and current data for West Africa were obtained from FEWS.net (downloaded 23 April 2018).
2) Data were clipped by UN OCHA boundaries for Nigeria, obtained from HDX data.humdata.org (downloaded 23 April 2018).
name: nigeria-fewsnet-ipc-acute-food-security-classifications-over-time-2009-2018
notes: This report explores food insecurity in Nigeria in the context of urbanization and demographic change.  A comparison of changing acute food security measures (IPC) from January and February 2010-2018  accompanies the report. The authors, Jordan Burnett, Leah Nadel, Victoria Santiago, and Arline Tarazona, completed their research in partial fulfillment of Public Health coursework in Medical Geography, for Spring 2018, at Drew University. Dr. Lisa Jordan edited the report and supplemented their work with additional spatial data.
title: Nigeria - FEWSNET IPC Acute Food Security Classifications over Time: A Public Health and Food Security Synthesis Report with Corresponding Data

resources.description:
FEWS NET IPC Acute Food Security Classification for Nigeria (2009-2018) stored as shapefiles, by year and month (3-4 times annually).  
Attributes(s): 
CS: Current Status (IPC Value 1-5, or 99 for missing data or not monitored)
HA0: the value 1 indicates that the situation would be worse on the IPC scale if not for humanitarian aid, 0 otherwise
